notes: Inbound SMB lead — early product-market fit for automated support chat. Team: CTO (Maya Alvarez), eng lead (Samir Patel). Primary complaint: inconsistent latency for EU customers causing UI flicker and perceived lag. They've been using single-region routing (eu-west-1) and default 60s client timeouts; front-end cancels requests if no bytes received for 3s. On call: recommended immediate changes: enable streaming responses, lower client cancel threshold to 8s for first byte, set request timeout to 30s for chat endpoints, and add token budget per message (truncate long history on client). Also suggested region routing policy: route EU traffic to closest region but failover to us-west-2 when p99 exceeds 1.5x SLA. Customer quote: "We see good quality but UI feels sluggish — need quick wins before scaling." Provided links: pricing deck, quick tuning checklist. They are cost sensitive but prioritize end-user latency over small cost increases.
requirements_summary: Workload: multi-tenant support chat + document search. Latency targets: median <300ms token-response for short prompts, p95 <1200ms for chat turns. Throughput: 30 concurrent active users initially (spiky). Model: prefer open/quantized models; willing to try smaller fp16 variant for lower latency. Needs routing fallback, minimal setup (self-serve), SOC2 audit info.
